itinerary.cal: Best mid-July through September, once the high route beyond Buck Creek Pass and the basin have melted out; a free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is required and is available at the trailhead.

days.note: From the Trinity trailhead (2,800 ft) at the end of Chiwawa River Road, hike the Buck Creek Trail (No. 1513) about 9.6 miles and 3,100 ft to Buck Creek Pass, and fill up with water there. Follow the old High Pass trail around the west side of Liberty Cap and south to High Pass, where the tread fades into talus and snow, then contour through the pass and under Mount Berge and climb a short Class 3 step onto the ridge just south of Point 7839. An easy walk-off drops into Louis Creek Basin to camp. A long, dry, exposed day once past the pass.
days.title: Backpack in to Louis Creek Basin

schedule.label: Leave Trinity trailhead
schedule.detail: Buck Creek Trail No. 1513.

schedule.label: Buck Creek Pass (~5,800 ft)
schedule.detail: Last reliable water for about four miles; fill up.

schedule.label: High Pass
schedule.detail: Tread fades into talus and hard snow; crampons can help.

schedule.label: Louis Creek Basin camp
schedule.detail: Stay high on the traverse from the Berge saddle to avoid waterfall slabs.

days.objective: Reach camp in Louis Creek Basin below Buck's southwest side

days.note: Climb with a light pack from the basin: broad pumice, talus and low-angle snow lead up the south and southwest slopes to the crest, then loose, slabby schist with a short Class 3-4 step near a horn below the top. The crest has several bumps of nearly equal height, so walk it to find the high point. Return the same way to camp.
days.title: Summit Buck Mountain

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Early start to beat afternoon thunderstorm risk.

schedule.label: Gain the crest (~7,400 ft)
schedule.detail: Pumice, talus and low-angle snow.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 schist, locally 3-4 near a horn below the top.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Downclimb carefully; the schist is loose.

days.objective: Climb Buck Mountain (8,534 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the approach: back over the ridge south of Point 7839, under Mount Berge and through High Pass, around Liberty Cap to Buck Creek Pass, then down the Buck Creek Trail to Trinity. Carry enough water for the dry stretch before the pass.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Trinity trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day backpack of roughly 30 miles round trip: a long first day over Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass high route to a camp in Louis Creek Basin, a summit day of about four hours round trip from camp, and a long walk out. Buck is remote and lightly visited; expect loose rock, route-finding and a dry ridge rather than a trail.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200) to Trinity Trailhead
road.status: Closed beyond MP 18.2 (2026 season) — not a normal seasonal closure
road.driveNote: From Coles Corner (US-2) take SR-207 toward Lake Wenatchee ~4.2 mi, bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then left onto Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200); pavement ends near mile 10.8, and the final stretch is rough gravel/dirt not suited to low-clearance vehicles. Since May 20, 2026 the road has been closed to vehicles at MP 18.2 beyond Atkinson Flat Campground under Forest Service order 06-17-07-2026-11 (through December 31, 2027) — plan for extra road-walking miles to reach Trinity Trailhead. While the Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40) is in force, September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, the road and the Buck Creek Trail are closed to all entry.
road.seasonalGate: Normally opens as snow clears in late May/June and stays open into fall; currently closed beyond Atkinson Flat under USFS closure order #06-17-07-2026-11 (effective May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027 unless rescinded sooner) after December 2025 storm damage, rather than a routine seasonal gate.

itinerary.cal: Best July-October; trail holds snow into early summer and the upper basin is a popular fall-larch destination in late September/early October.

days.note: Standard single-day outing from the Phelps Creek trailhead: a steep, sustained climb through forest to an open basin around 6,100 ft, then a final push up open slopes/ridge to the summit. Descend the same trail. No camping — nearly everyone does this car-to-car.
days.title: Car-to-car day hike/scramble

schedule.label: Leave Phelps Creek trailhead
schedule.detail: Start on the wide Phelps Creek Trail.

schedule.label: Bear right onto Carne Mountain Trail
schedule.detail: Trail narrows and climbs steeply immediately.

schedule.label: Reach the basin (~6,100 ft)
schedule.detail: Open mountain basin with campsites and a stream; grade eases briefly.

schedule.label: Final push to summit ridge and top
schedule.detail: Open slopes/talus to the 7,091 ft summit; class 2 scrambling near the top in places.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 360-degree views of Clark, Buck, Glacier, Fortress, Chiwawa, Dumbell, Bonanza, Seven-Fingered Jack, and Maude.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse the trail; ~2.5-3 hr descent.

days.objective: Summit Carne Mountain (7,091 ft) via the Carne Mountain Trail

itinerary.totalNote: A single, long day hike/scramble: roughly 6-7 hours car-to-car, ~7.6-8 miles round trip with 3,600 ft gain — no overnight camp needed.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: Closed as of May 20, 2026 (USFS Forest Order #06-17-07-2026-11): FR 6200 is closed to vehicles at milepost 18.2, just past Atkinson Flat Campground, after a debris flow deposited roughly 150 cubic yards of material and cut ruts near the Dry Creek Bridge. No reopening estimate has been given; the order runs effective May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027 unless rescinded sooner. Check the Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts page before driving — the Phelps Creek Trailhead is unreachable by vehicle beyond this closure. The Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes Phelps Creek Road and the Carne Mountain Trail.
road.driveNote: From Coles Corner on US-2 (about 15 miles west of Leavenworth), take WA-207 north ~4.4 miles, bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road for 0.4 mile, then right onto County Hwy 22/Chiwawa River Road for 0.8 mile to Forest Road 6200. Continue north on FR 6200 about 22 miles (paved for roughly the first half, then rough gravel) to FR 6211, then turn right and drive the rough, potholed Phelps Creek Road 2.3 miles to the trailhead (3,500 ft). Low-clearance vehicles should go slowly on the upper roads.
road.seasonalGate: Not gated, but the upper road and trailhead are typically snow-covered and impractical until roughly June; check current USFS road/trail conditions.

itinerary.cal: The route holds snow into summer, so most ascents happen late June through September.

days.note: From the Chiwawa River / Trinity trailhead (2,800 ft), follow Chiwawa River Trail #1550 along the old Red Mountain mining road, passing the Buck Creek and Chiwawa Basin trail junctions around 4,800 ft. The lower trail is brushy/overgrown in summer; expect a long, steady climb through forest into open basin terrain for camp.
days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp near 5,900-6,300 ft on the old Red Mountain mining road

days.note: From camp, cross crusty morning snow slopes up to the broad saddle near 7,200 ft between Chiwawa and Fortress, then work up the southwest snowfield/talus with a short Class 2-3 ledge traverse to the summit ridge. Many parties tag Fortress Mountain's Class 3-4 east ridge from the same col on the same day.
days.title: Summit day: Chiwawa Mountain via SW snowfield

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Cross firm morning snow before it softens.

schedule.label: Reach Chiwawa-Fortress saddle (~7,200 ft)
schedule.detail: Broad, gently inclined snow ramp leads to the col.

schedule.label: Southwest snowfield and ledge traverse
schedule.detail: Class 2+ ledges round the south rib onto the SW slopes.

schedule.label: Summit (8,459 ft)
schedule.detail: Typical summit arrival on a full-value day.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Descend the same snow/talus line; glissade where safe.

days.objective: Climb Chiwawa Mountain (8,459 ft) and return to high camp

days.note: Retrace the Red Mountain mining road/Chiwawa River Trail back down through the brushy lower miles to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Chiwawa River trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-3 day trip for most parties: ~19-20 miles round trip with roughly 5,700 ft cumulative gain/loss; camp sits near 5,900-6,300 ft on the old mining road, with a long (7+ hr) summit push on day two. Very strong parties have done it car-to-car in a single ~14-16 hr day.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road / Forest Road 6200
road.status: paved for roughly the first 8-11 miles from Chiwawa Loop Road, then rough gravel/dirt for the final ~10-12 miles to Trinity Trailhead
road.driveNote: From Coles Corner on US-2, take WA-207 north 4.4 miles, then Chiwawa Loop Road and FR 6200 about 23 miles total to Trinity Trailhead (2,800'); the final stretch is not recommended for low-clearance vehicles.
road.seasonalGate: Usually not fully accessible until the road melts out/is cleared, often mid-to-late June. The road is additionally closed from Atkinson Flats Campground north to Trinity under Forest Service order 06-17-07-2026-11 (effective May 20, 2026 through Dec 31, 2027), due to December 2025 storm damage — Trinity Trailhead is NOT reachable by vehicle. The Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes the road and the Chiwawa River Trail. Check Wenatchee River Ranger District alerts before driving.

itinerary.cal: Glacier Peak Wilderness requires a free self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead. The Phelps Creek approach crosses the permanent snowfield below Spider Gap in both directions, so carry an ice axe and traction. Longer alternatives reach Cloudy Pass from Trinity over Buck Creek Pass or from Holden Village up Railroad Creek.

days.note: Drive to the Phelps Creek Trailhead and follow Trail #1511 up the valley to Spider Meadow, then climb through upper Phelps Basin and up the permanent snowfield to Spider Gap. Drop down the north side past the Lyman Glacier and Upper Lyman Lakes to Lower Lyman Lake, then climb the meadows to Cloudy Pass — camp at Lower Lyman Lake or up at the pass itself.
days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach Lyman Lake / Cloudy Pass camp

days.note: Leave camp with a light pack and climb from Cloudy Pass up open slopes to gain the southwest ridge, then follow the ridge to the summit block. The final moves are class 3-4 on the block itself — most parties traverse to its north side to find the easiest weakness, and some choose to belay the last few moves.
days.title: Summit day (scramble)

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light day pack from Lyman Lake/Cloudy Pass camp.

schedule.label: Cloudy Pass
schedule.detail: Leave the trail here, angle northeast up open slopes.

schedule.label: Gain southwest ridge
schedule.detail: Follow social boot-tracks up loose but non-technical terrain.

schedule.label: Reach summit block
schedule.detail: Traverse to the north side for the class 3-4 finish; some parties rope up here.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 7,915 ft — views of Glacier Peak, Bonanza Peak, and the Lyman Lakes basin.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge and pass, downclimbing the block first.

days.objective: Climb the Southwest Slopes/ridge to the 7,915 ft summit block

days.note: Pack up and retrace the approach: down to Lower Lyman Lake, back up and over Spider Gap, and down Phelps Creek Trail #1511 to the Phelps Creek Trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Phelps Creek Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip for most parties: roughly 31 miles and ~7,550 ft of gain round trip from the Phelps Creek Trailhead over Spider Gap, with a single scramble day (class 3-4 at the summit block) done from a Lyman Lake/Cloudy Pass camp.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FSR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FSR 6211)/Phelps Creek Trailhead, or FSR 6200 to Trinity Trailhead; alternatively no road needed via the Lake Chelan ferry + Holden Village approach
road.status: Closed since May 20, 2026: FSR 6200 is closed from the Atkinson Flat Campground junction north to Trinity under Forest Service order 06-17-07-2026-11 (through December 31, 2027), cutting off both Phelps Creek and Trinity trailheads from this side; the Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes FSR 6200 and the Phelps Creek Trail
road.driveNote: When open: from Leavenworth, US-2 W 15 mi to Coles Corner, WA-207 N 4.4 mi, Chiwawa Loop Rd, then FSR 6200 ~22 mi (gravel after mile 11) to Phelps Creek Rd/FSR 6211, then 2.3 mi to Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft). Rough, rutted road, not recommended for low-clearance vehicles even when fully open.

itinerary.cal: Leroy Creek's crossing is most difficult during early-summer snowmelt; a snow-filled couloir on the route can hold a firm, refrigerated finger of snow into mid-summer, and afternoon thunderstorms are common so an early start/turnaround matters.

days.note: From the Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft), follow the Phelps Creek Trail about 3.5 miles to the Leroy Creek crossing (the third and hardest ford), then climb a steep, unmaintained climber's path north of the creek to the flat basin at ~6,100 ft that serves as the standard camp. Water, flat tent sites, and views of the southwest slopes are all right at camp.
days.title: Approach to Leroy Basin camp

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: 3,500 ft, Phelps Creek Trailhead.

schedule.label: Cross Leroy Creek
schedule.detail: Third major creek crossing on the Phelps Creek Trail; can be tricky in high water.

schedule.label: Arrive Leroy Basin camp
schedule.detail: Flat basin at ~6,100 ft below the southwest slopes.

days.objective: Establish camp at Leroy Basin (~6,100 ft)

days.note: Leave camp early to beat afternoon thunderstorms and soften scree; ascend via either the rock gully or the gentler ridge to its right, both converging on the broad southwest slope, then trend left near the summit block to reach the true (leftmost) summit. Basin-to-summit is roughly 3 hours; after the summit, break camp and hike all the way back to the trailhead the same day.
days.title: Summit push and hike out

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light summit pack; early start avoids afternoon storms and loose scree becoming unstable in the heat.

schedule.label: Reach summit
schedule.detail: ~3 hrs from Leroy Basin per multiple trip reports; loose talus/scree the whole way, helmet recommended.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent route; descent to the basin is noticeably faster than the climb (often under an hour).

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Break camp and pack up.

schedule.label: Start hike out
schedule.detail: Reverse Day 1's route back to the trailhead.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Total round trip from camp: roughly 8 miles, 8,600 ft combined gain/loss.

days.objective: Climb Seven Fingered Jack via the Southwest Slopes, then break camp and hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night overnight trip: ~13 miles and 5,600 ft gain round trip, with the standard camp at Leroy Basin (6,100 ft) and about 3 hours basin-to-summit on loose scree and talus.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: Roughly 22 miles on FR 6200 (paved near the valley, gravel/rough further in) then about 2.3-2.5 miles on FR 6211 to road's end at the Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft); rough native-surface sections are not recommended for low-clearance vehicles. FR 6200 has been closed to vehicles at milepost 18.2 (just past Atkinson Flat Campground) due to storm/debris-flow damage near the Dry Creek Bridge since May 20, 2026, under Forest Service order 06-17-07-2026-11, which runs through at least December 31, 2027 with no reopening estimate — this closure blocks the standard drive-to-trailhead approach and adds significant road-walking distance. The Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes FR 6200, Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211) and the Phelps Creek Trail. Verify current status with the Ranger District before driving.
road.driveNote: From Leavenworth: US-2 west ~15 mi to Coles Corner, right on WA-207 north ~4.4 mi, right on Chiwawa Loop Rd (stay right at the intersection), then left onto Chiwawa River Rd/FR 6200 for ~22 mi, then right onto Phelps Creek Rd/FR 6211 for ~2.3-2.5 mi to the trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Typically opens late spring once snow and washouts are cleared; closes with the first significant fall/winter snow

itinerary.cal: Best late July-September; the upper basin holds snow into July and the scramble ledges are safer dry, though an axe is still handy even in late season.

days.note: An easy, well-graded cruise up the Phelps Creek Trail through Spider Meadow, then a rougher push into upper Phelps Basin where the trail peters out to a bootpath. Camp here (rather than lower Spider Meadow) shortens summit day considerably.
days.title: Hike in to Upper Phelps Basin
days.objective: Establish camp near ~6,000 ft (established bivy sites cluster 5,700-6,100 ft)

days.note: From camp, ascend the talus basin south of the peak to a notch just west of the summit, pick through two short cliff bands (the second via a dirty gully on the left, then class 2 ledges), then follow the ridge - easy but airy class 3 - to the top. Many parties tag Greenwood Mountain too via a connecting summit ledge before returning to camp the same way.
days.title: Climb Dumbell Mountain

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light scramble pack; axe recommended even late season.

schedule.label: Reach base of the talus basin
schedule.detail: Ascend the drainage or the slope just north of it toward the notch.

schedule.label: Cliff bands
schedule.detail: Second band is the crux - dirty gully on the left leads to class 2 ledges up to the notch.

schedule.label: Gain the ridge notch
schedule.detail: Follow the ridge crest, or traverse just below on the north side, to the summit.

schedule.label: Summit Dumbell
schedule.detail: 3-4 hrs up from upper basin per route reports; optionally continue to Greenwood via the connecting ledge.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent line; descent runs faster than the ascent.

days.objective: Summit Dumbell (8,416 ft) via the Southwest Slope-South Face scramble

days.note: Reverse the approach through upper Phelps Basin and Spider Meadow back down the Phelps Creek Trail to the car.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Phelps Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day backpack is the common recommended plan (~17 mi, ~5,000 ft gain round trip); very strong parties do combine it into one long car-to-car day (~10.5-11 hrs), often tagging neighboring Greenwood Mountain too.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: paved to Chiwawa Loop Road, then gravel/rough forest road; final 2.3 miles very rough -- closed as of the 2026 season beyond Atkinson Flat Campground under an active USFS storm-damage closure order (in effect through at least Dec 31, 2027)
road.driveNote: From Coles Corner take WA-207 north, then Chiwawa Loop Road, then Chiwawa River Road/FR 6200 for about 22 miles, then right on Phelps Creek Road/FR 6211 for 2.3 miles to the trailhead (~3,500 ft). The Railroad Creek/Lyman Lake side is reached separately via boat or trail from Lake Chelan to Holden Village — a much longer alternate approach, not the standard route to Dumbell.
road.seasonalGate: Not gated in a normal year, but the road has been closed to vehicles beyond Atkinson Flat Campground since May 20, 2026 for storm/debris-flow damage, under Forest Service order 06-17-07-2026-11, which runs through December 31, 2027, and the Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect from September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211) and the Phelps Creek Trail — this blocks the standard drive to the Phelps Creek Trailhead. In normal open years it is also subject to lingering snow on the upper road/trail into June.

itinerary.cal: Glacier Peak Wilderness requires a free self-issue permit at the trailhead; the high route and basin are typically not fully snow-free until mid-to-late July.

days.note: From the Trinity Trailhead, walk the Chiwawa River Trail upstream about 4 miles to the unsigned Massie Lake junction (a large boulder on one side of the trail, an 'M' with an arrow carved in a tree on the other). Ford the river there and climb the steep, faint old sheep path about 2 miles to Massie Lake. Fill up at the river: there is no dependable water between the ford and the lake. Camp at the lake.
days.title: Approach to Massie Lake
days.objective: Reach Massie Lake (about 5,900 ft) and set up camp

days.note: From the lake, follow the faint high-route tread away from the basin, leave it and climb onto Massie Peak's broad west ridge, then follow the crest to the summit on talus and heather with a few short class 3 steps. Reverse the same line to camp, pack up, and walk back down the sheep path, across the ford and out the Chiwawa River Trail. The sheep path is easiest to lose on the way down.
days.title: Summit Massie Peak and hike out

schedule.label: Leave Massie Lake camp
schedule.detail: Day pack only; carry all your water for the climb.

schedule.label: Gain the west ridge
schedule.detail: Leave the faint high-route tread and turn uphill onto the ridge.

schedule.label: Summit Massie Peak (7,533 ft)
schedule.detail: Short class 3 steps near the top.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge; break camp.

schedule.label: Back at Trinity Trailhead
schedule.detail: Down the sheep path, across the ford, out the Chiwawa River Trail.

days.objective: Climb the West Route and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night trip: about 6 miles and 3,100 ft up the Chiwawa River Trail and the old sheep path to camp at Massie Lake (about 5,900 ft), then the summit by the west ridge and the walk out, about 9 miles. Strong parties do the whole thing car-to-car in one long day.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200)
road.status: Paved near Lake Wenatchee, transitioning to rough washboard gravel/dirt for roughly the final 12 miles to the Trinity/Phelps Creek trailheads; passable to most vehicles in dry conditions but slow going for low-clearance cars. Closed to vehicles beyond the Atkinson Flat Campground junction since May 20, 2026 for storm damage (Okanogan-Wenatchee order 06-17-07-2026-11, in effect through December 31, 2027, no reopening estimate), which cuts off the Trinity and Phelps Creek trailheads. The Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40) also closes the Chiwawa River Road and Phelps Creek Road through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner. Check with the Wenatchee River Ranger District, (509) 548-2550, before you go.
road.driveNote: From Leavenworth: US-2 west ~15 mi to Coles Corner, WA-207 north 4.4 mi, then Chiwawa River Rd (FR 6200) up-valley to the Trinity/Phelps Creek trailheads.

itinerary.cal: Best climbed July-September once the Leroy Basin slabs/talus and summit block are snow-free; Phelps Creek Rd (FR 6211) opens with spring snowmelt, typically by June.

days.note: Flat forested trail along Phelps Creek for about 3.5 miles, then a steep climber's path gaining roughly 2,000 ft in 1.5 miles up into Leroy Basin. Camp at the large meadow (~6,100 ft) with good water, about a mile southwest of Seven Fingered Jack.
days.title: Approach to Leroy Basin camp
days.objective: Reach Leroy Creek Camp

days.note: The long day of the trip: cross Gloomy Basin and a loose moraine saddle, follow water-polished slabs then grueling loose talus toward the final wall, then tackle the exposed class 4 summit block (many parties hand-line or belay it). Round trip from camp typically runs 10-12 hours; the return leg is nearly as slow as the ascent due to the loose terrain.
days.title: Summit push and return to camp

schedule.label: Leave Leroy Creek Camp
schedule.detail: Early start is key given the length of the day ahead.

schedule.label: Cross Gloomy Basin/moraine saddle
schedule.detail: Loose talus traverse toward Fernow's east side.

schedule.label: Reach base of summit block
schedule.detail: Water-polished slabs give way to loose talus below the final wall.

schedule.label: Summit (9,249 ft)
schedule.detail: Exposed class 4 summit block is the technical crux of the route.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Down-climb or belay the summit block, then reverse the basin traverse.

schedule.label: Back at Leroy Creek Camp
schedule.detail: Many parties finish in fading light on this leg — carry a headlamp.

days.objective: Climb the Southeast Face to Fernow's summit and back to camp

days.note: Reverse the Day 1 approach: down the steep Leroy Basin climber's path and back out the flat Phelps Creek trail to the car.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Phelps Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~17.5-mile round-trip backpack with about 8,100 ft of cumulative gain, most of it on a grueling 10-12 hour summit day over loose talus and an exposed class 4 summit block; strong parties occasionally compress the whole thing into a single ~18-20 hour car-to-car day instead.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: Closed to vehicles beyond Atkinson Flat Campground since May 20, 2026 for storm damage, under Forest Service order 06-17-07-2026-11, which runs through December 31, 2027; the Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect from September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes FR 6200, Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211) and the Phelps Creek and Leroy Creek trails.
road.driveNote: When open: from Coles Corner on US-2, go north on WA-207 ~4.4 mi, right on Chiwawa Loop Rd, then FR 6200 (Chiwawa River Rd) ~22 rough gravel/dirt miles, then right on FR 6211 (Phelps Creek Rd) 2.3 mi to the trailhead (3,500 ft). High-clearance vehicle recommended even when fully open.
road.seasonalGate: Not a normal seasonal gate; the current closure is a storm-damage order running through December 31, 2027, not a winter gate.

itinerary.cal: Best climbed in a firm-snow window (typically June to mid-July) — later in the season the north-facing snow degrades to scree/rotten ice and the face gets considerably harder and looser.

days.note: A pre-dawn start up the Phelps Creek and Leroy Creek trails to the basin, then up to the Seven Fingered Jack-Maude col to rope up and gear up before climbing sustained 35-45 degree snow on the North Face to the summit ridge. Descend south over the summit and down the broad south slopes/talus back into Leroy Basin and out the same trail.
days.title: Car-to-car: Leroy Creek approach, North Face, South Slopes descent

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Phelps Creek trail by headlamp.

schedule.label: Reach Leroy Creek Basin
schedule.detail: Meadow camp area at ~6,100 ft; refill water.

schedule.label: Reach the Seven Fingered Jack-Maude col
schedule.detail: Rope up, crampons and tools on for the face.

schedule.label: Begin climbing the North Face
schedule.detail: Sustained 35-45 degree snow.

schedule.label: Top out onto the summit ridge
schedule.detail: Low-angle terrain to the true summit; lunch and rest.

schedule.label: Descend via South Slopes
schedule.detail: Back through Leroy Basin (~4:00 PM) to the car by ~6:15 PM.

days.objective: Climb the North Face and descend via the South Slopes to close the loop

itinerary.totalNote: A very long but standard single push: strong parties climb the North Face car-to-car in about 12-13 hours via Leroy Creek Basin, descending the South Slopes on the far side of the mountain back to the same trailhead — roughly 14 miles and ~5,600-6,000 ft of gain/loss.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road / Phelps Creek Road
road.status: Unpaved, rough and washboarded; high-clearance vehicle recommended. Closed to vehicles beyond the Atkinson Flat Campground junction since May 20, 2026 for storm damage (Okanogan-Wenatchee order 06-17-07-2026-11, in effect through December 31, 2027, no reopening estimate), which cuts off the Trinity and Phelps Creek trailheads. The Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40) also closes the Chiwawa River Road and Phelps Creek Road through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner. Check with the Wenatchee River Ranger District, (509) 548-2550, before you go.
road.driveNote: Long gravel forest roads to the Phelps Creek / Chiwawa trailheads

itinerary.cal: Best climbed July-September once the scree ramp and stream-bed crux are snow-free.

days.note: Hike the Phelps Creek Trail then break off onto the Leroy climbers' path, which steepens sharply (around 1,200 ft/mile) into Leroy Basin. Parties report going through several liters of water on this leg in afternoon heat; camp in the trees away from the busier lakeside sites.
days.title: Approach to high camp

schedule.label: Leave Phelps Creek trailhead
schedule.detail: ~3,500 ft; well-graded trail for the first ~3.5 miles.

schedule.label: Turn off onto Leroy climbers' path
schedule.detail: About 1.5 hrs from the trailhead to the Leroy High Route junction.

schedule.label: Arrive Leroy Basin camp
schedule.detail: ~6,100 ft; steep final push, plan for a hot, exposed climb with a full overnight pack.

days.objective: Reach Leroy Basin camp

days.note: A long day: cross Leroy Pass and Freezer Pass, drop into the Ice Lakes basin, then traverse a loose, consequential stream-bed crux before gaining the southwest ridge on a scree ramp. The scrambling above is chossy class 3 (feels like low class 4 with the exposure) with several one-at-a-time sections to avoid rockfall.
days.title: Summit push via Freezer Pass and the SW ridge

schedule.label: Wake, leave camp before/at sunrise
schedule.detail: Light packs; leave the overnight gear at Leroy Basin.

schedule.label: Freezer Pass, drop into Ice Lakes basin
schedule.detail: Cross-country traverse, ~500 ft down to the basin.

schedule.label: Stream-bed crux
schedule.detail: Loose clay/scree gully — tricky down-climb and re-ascent, reported as the route's toughest obstacle.

schedule.label: Gain the southwest ridge
schedule.detail: ~400 ft up a scree/talus ramp to the ridge crest.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 ledges and gendarmes on the final push; trip reports place summit arrival early-to-mid afternoon.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the full line; budget 7+ hours round trip from camp.

days.objective: Climb South Spectacle Butte (8,392 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and retrace the Leroy climbers' path and Phelps Creek Trail back to the car.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~21-mile round trip with a long class 3-4 summit day out of a Leroy Basin high camp; ~7,500 ft of cumulative gain, most of it on day 2.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: Paved/gravel Chiwawa Loop Road transitions to gravel/dirt FR 6200 beyond about mile 11, then FR 6211 for the final ~2.3 miles — rough and rutted, not suitable for low-clearance vehicles; roughly 14 miles of rough dirt/gravel total. Closed to vehicles beyond the Atkinson Flat Campground junction since May 20, 2026 for storm damage (Okanogan-Wenatchee order 06-17-07-2026-11, in effect through December 31, 2027, no reopening estimate), which cuts off the Trinity and Phelps Creek trailheads. The Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40) also closes the Chiwawa River Road and Phelps Creek Road through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner. Check with the Wenatchee River Ranger District, (509) 548-2550, before you go.
road.driveNote: From Leavenworth: US-2 west ~15 mi to Coles Corner, WA-207 north ~4.4 mi, then Chiwawa Loop Road to Chiwawa River Rd/FR 6200 for ~22 mi, then FR 6211 ~2.3 mi to the Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft).
road.seasonalGate: Typically snowed shut from late fall through spring; opening date varies by year and is further affected by storm-damage closures — check Wenatchee River Ranger District road/trail alerts before driving.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road / FR 6200
road.status: Open to Atkinson Flat Campground (~mile 16); closed to vehicles beyond that point to Trinity Trailhead under USFS order #06-17-07-2026-11 (effective May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027 unless rescinded sooner) after December 2025 storm damage. The Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes FR 6200 and the Chiwawa River Trail
road.driveNote: Same access as the Southwest Face route: from Coles Corner on US-2, WA-207 north, then Chiwawa Loop Road and Chiwawa River Road/FR 6200 ~23 mi to Trinity Trailhead. Under the storm-damage closure, park near Atkinson Flat and walk the final ~7 miles each way; while the Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40) is in force, September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, FR 6200 is closed to all entry, so this walk is not open.
road.seasonalGate: Normally opens as snow clears, typically by June in an average year, once the current storm-damage closure is lifted; the final 12 miles are rough, native-surface road unsuitable for low-clearance vehicles even when open

road.driveNote: From US-2/SR-207 near Lake Wenatchee, follow Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) about 22 miles, then turn right on Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211) and continue ~2.3-2.5 miles to the trailhead (3,500 ft).
road.seasonalGate: Typically snow-free and drivable late May/June through fall; subject to storm-damage closures - check current Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts before driving
